newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mint tender points to lower zinc premiums.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mint tender points to lower zinc premiums.

text.p: The U.S. Mint tender for 1,900 tonnes of special high grade zinc points to lower zinc premiums, dipping below the 5.00 cent level for the first time in many months, dealers said.

The winning sellers of metal were expected to be Phoenixx International with 1,050 tonnes at premiums of 4.4 to 4.6 cents per pound over LME cash, Hochschild Partners, 204 tonnes at 4.85 cents, and Ore & Chemical (MG), 640 tonnes at 4.93 cents.
Zinc premiums had been in the 5.00 to 5.50 cents per pound range in recent weeks, dipping to 5.00 to 5.25 by last week.
"I guess the premiums are going lower," a dealer said.
Another merchant added: "This indicates to me that the premiums are now 4.75 to 5.00 cents."
